purpose: PRE-REGISTRATION of the Phase-2 nested-hindcast design. Written BEFORE any effect-side research (closure timestamps, gauge peaks, warning times) was read by the orchestrator. Every choice below is cause-side: terrain, QPE, road/stream geometry, standard engineering thresholds. Nothing here may be changed after effect data is read, except compute-budget coarsening of dx, which must be logged with its reason.

franklinton.notes: buildings as closed cells if footprint data reachable; floodwall present in LiDAR

pataskala.role: flash-pluvial / small-channel / road-crossing test; includes US-40 (National Road) corridor through Etna for the detour analysis

buckeye.role: South Fork Licking + Buckeye Lake + I-70 embankment / SR-79 crossing hydraulics

forcing.operational_replay: MRMS RadarOnly QPE (QPE-A, 15-min if available) — used for lead-time analysis; solver is causal so a single QPE-A-forced run IS a chronological replay; QPE-A product latency (~2 min) is added when quoting warning times
forcing.no_calibration: QPE is never scaled/corrected using flood observations; gauge-vs-QPE bias is reported, not applied
sim_window_utc: 2026-08-20T12:00Z minimum; extended to cover QPE rain end + 4 h drain-down

infiltration_ensemble.I0: 0 mm/hr (saturated antecedent bound) — primary, all runs
infiltration_ensemble.I1: 3 mm/hr constant (saturated clay-loam steady rate) — sensitivity, pataskala nest + parent
infiltration_ensemble.I2: soil-derived — only if a reachable soils dataset is found; else declared not run

boundary_conditions.method: Dirichlet stage strips on nest edges taken from the 60 m parent QPE-B run, recorded at <=5-min cadence at nest boundary cells; nests also receive full QPE rain-on-grid
boundary_conditions.franklinton_caveat: parent domain ends at 40.20N; Scioto/Olentangy inflow generated north of that is NOT represented — mainstem stage will be biased low; declared, not tuned

hydraulic_geometry_policy.culverts: at each TIGER road x NHD flowline crossing where the DTM shows a continuous embankment (no open water gap along the flowline), add an orifice connection with cd_area = 1.5 m^2 (typical single box culvert), crest = embankment top; bridges (gaps already present in bare-earth DTM) are left as-is
hydraulic_geometry_policy.buildings: closed no-flow cells where footprint coverage >= 0.5 and dx <= 10 m, if footprint data reachable
hydraulic_geometry_policy.no_effect_tuning: no geometry, roughness, or threshold may be adjusted using observed flood locations/timings

road_inundation_thresholds.basis: FHWA/NWS guidance: ~12 in of moving water floats passenger vehicles
road_inundation_thresholds.warning_definition: t_warn(road segment) = first model time when >= 3 contiguous carriageway cells exceed impassable_m
segments_of_record: I-70 at SR-79 / South Fork Licking crossing
SR-310 Main St Pataskala incl. South Fork crossing

scoring_definitions.gauge_comparison: for any USGS gauge inside a nest: model water-surface stage at gauge cell vs observed stage; report rise-limb RMSE, peak error (m), time-to-peak error (min), threshold-crossing timing error (min); observed datum offset handled by comparing RISE above pre-event baseline, not absolute stage
scoring_definitions.lead_time: LeadTime_i = T_observed_impact_i - T_model_warning_i using QPE-A replay; negative lead times reported as-is
scoring_definitions.extent: qualitative overlay + wet-area fraction per corridor; no threshold retuning

amendments.utc: before any effect-side agent results were read
amendments.reason: compute budget: 4 CPU cores / 15 GB RAM; NumPy single-core throughput ~2e7 cell-steps/s makes 4-5 m nests (>8e11 cell-steps) infeasible in-session

changes.nest_frame_interval: 3600 s (timing analysis uses 60 s probes, not frames)
changes.sim_window: t0 = first QPE interval with AOI-mean rate > 0.5 mm/h minus 1 h; end = last wet interval + 4 h drain-down; cap 16 h

amendments.note: driven purely by hardware; no effect data consulted

amendments.utc: after gauge-agent return, before any effect-side (closure/warning) research was read
amendments.reason: include the S Fork Licking blw Kirkersville gauged reach (03144816, 39.964 -82.595) inside the pataskala nest as a timing anchor; gauge LOCATION is infrastructure (cause-side) — its observed series stays unread until scoring
amendments.note: observed hydrograph source is NWM analysis_assim (USGS-assimilated) because direct USGS endpoints are egress-blocked; labeled as such in scoring

amendments.utc: AFTER effect research was read — declared transparently
amendments.reason: the I-70/Buckeye Lake closure was driven by the SLOW fluvial crest of the South Fork Licking (observed crest ~Aug 21 midday, ~43-46 h after model t0), far beyond the pre-registered 26 h cap. Extending the simulated window is justified by basin-routing first principles (a ~700 km^2 basin with in-line lake storage has >24 h lag); a longer window cannot steer the model toward the observed answer — it only lets the model's own dynamics play out. No forcing, geometry, roughness or threshold was changed.

changes.parent_extended_run: run_qpeB_parent_ext with cap 56 h (rain unchanged; ends 13Z Aug 20; everything after is pure routing)

amendments.flag: this amendment postdates effect exposure and is labeled as such in all reporting

amendments.finding: the scalar drainage term (storm-sewer proxy, 5 mm/hr effective) linearly drains routed river water — the extended parent's I-70/South Fork probe decays at exactly 0.005 m/hr after the flash peak instead of rising to the observed Aug 21 fluvial crest. Structural cause identified BEFORE seeing any nest result: multi-day river routing was never in this term's design scope (also absent: baseflow, upstream-of-domain inflow, Buckeye Lake dam/spillway operations).
amendments.action: the pre-registered buckeye nest runs unchanged (drainage on); an additional SENSITIVITY member run_nest_buckeye_B_ext_nodrain disables the drain proxy to isolate how much of the missing crest that term explains. Labeled post-hoc sensitivity — never merged into the primary scoring.
amendments.flag: post-effect, hypothesis-driven sensitivity; primary scoring remains the pre-registered configuration

amendments.utc: compute amendment #4 — measured infeasibility, not a scientific choice
amendments.reason: the wide nests were killed after measurement showed the storm-phase CFL cost is unaffordable: frame intervals grew 0.2 -> 29.5 -> 101.2 min as the parent's deep river stage reached the nest boundaries (dt = cfl*dx/sqrt(g*h) collapses below 1 s, ~5000 steps per simulated hour over 1.5-3M cells). Remaining work measured at 30-100+ h per nest on 4 cores.

changes.domains: corridor extents replace wide extents; RESOLUTION IS PRESERVED (6 m; pataskala 8 m) — extent was cut rather than physics resolution, the lesser compromise
changes.bc: boundary stages reconstructed from completed parent FRAMES (30-min cadence) rather than the 300 s live record, since the live record only covers the original wide perimeters; cadence limitation recorded in each BC file

amendments.scientific_justification_for_the_22h_win: the Case A vs Case B discriminator does NOT require the Aug 21 fluvial crest. The parent claimed 'I-70 impassable' at model hour 16.4 (10:25Z Aug 20). Whether that signal is real road inundation or 60 m smearing of adjacent channel water is decided AT THAT MOMENT, by comparing carriageway cells against channel cells at 6 m. That is a 0-22 h question. The separate question of whether the model can reproduce the delayed fluvial crest is already answered NEGATIVELY by the extended parent (drainage-proxy defect) and is reported as a limitation.
amendments.cost: franklinton_c loses the Scioto 03221646 gauge probe (outside the corridor); buckeye_c loses nothing after the north extension; wide partial output retained under run_nest_*_wide_partial
